Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl

Class AdHocToolProvider

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl.AdHocToolProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
dev.langchain4j.service.tool.ToolProvider
public class AdHocToolProvider extends Object implements dev.langchain4j.service.tool.ToolProvider
The tools of an agentic ad hoc sub process: one per startable child, plus completeScope. The activity is the tool — a wrong activity name is not expressible for the model, because there is no generic "start something" call to put it in.

Built from the parse-time catalogue on the scope's activity, so what the model is offered is exactly what the deployment validated. A tool's parameters are the toolParameter calls in its input mappings (CIB7-2136), and nothing else. Four things are refused before the activity starts, through the same exception channel every other tool error takes back to the model: a value the declaration does not name, a value of the wrong type, a text longer than the String variable that would hold it, and a call that leaves out a parameter the declaration makes required — the model reads the refusal and calls again.

The execution stays in AdHocSubProcessTool: this class only translates a tool call into that layer's startActivity/completeScope, which is where the per-turn call cap, the blocking rule and the completion bookkeeping live.

    • specification

      protected dev.langchain4j.agent.tool.ToolSpecification specification(AdHocToolDescriptor descriptor)
      The tool specification of one catalogue entry: the id as the name, the label and documentation as the description, the declared parameters as the schema.

      An optional parameter is simply absent from required — fine for the default, non-strict schema this connector sends today. OpenAI's strict tool mode requires every property to be listed in required (optionality is expressed by also making the type nullable); if this connector ever turns strict mode on, a declared-optional parameter stops being expressible as written here and this method needs revisiting, not just the request flag.

    • arguments

      protected Map<String,Object> arguments(AdHocToolDescriptor descriptor, String argumentsJson)
      The call's arguments, restricted to the declared parameters.

      An undeclared name is refused rather than dropped: silently dropping it would have the model believe the value arrived. Types were promised to the model in the schema; a value that still arrives with the wrong shape is refused, not coerced. A required parameter that is absent, or passed as null, is refused as well; an optional one is simply absent, and toolCall.<name> reads null.

      All of it is refused at once, before the activity starts, in one message through the exception channel: the model can fix the whole call in its next attempt rather than one mistake at a time.

    • missingRequiredParameters

      protected String missingRequiredParameters(AdHocToolDescriptor descriptor, Map<String,Object> values, List<String> refused)
      Why the call lacks a required parameter, or null: every required parameter missing from values or passed as null is named in one sentence. One passed with the wrong type, or with a text too long to store, is not missing; its refusal says so already. A variable of the same name visible on the scope does not stand in for it: the activity reads the value from toolCall, not from that variable.

    • variables

      protected Map<String,Object> variables(AdHocToolDescriptor descriptor, Map<String,Object> arguments)
      The variables one call sets on its performance (CIB7-2136): a tool that declares a parameter gets every argument in toolCall, which its input mapping reads as toolCall.<name>. No argument is set under its own name, so a process variable of that name stays visible. A tool without parameters gets no toolCall and no variable of its own from the call.

      toolCall is a Java-serialized TreeMap (AdHocToolDescriptor.toolCallValue(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>)): its serialized form does not depend on how the map was built, so reading it back in a later command does not write it again. A copied LinkedHashMap keeps a table sized for its entries, which deserialization rebuilds larger, so the engine's check for changed objects would see a change on every first read.

    • fitting

      protected String fitting(AdHocToolDescriptor descriptor, AdHocToolDescriptor.Parameter declared, String text)
      A text argument of a parameter the tool stores whole (AdHocToolDescriptor.Parameter.isStoredWhole()), as long as a String variable holds; a longer one refused, with its length and the limit, so that the model shortens it. Let through, the input would fail the step at the flush, and the step's retries would ask the model again each time and end in an incident. The limit is the one the agent's answer is kept within (AgenticTurnRunner.fitsAStringVariable(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)). A text the tool stores with more around it is not checked here: what it adds is known only when the input is evaluated.
